Two weights and a `relu` between them, written in the M0 subset: a `let` binding, nested operator calls and two parameters with one canonical path each. [Write a model](../guides/write-a-model.mdx) builds it step by step.

The output below was recorded by `modelspec-docs` running the `modelspec` command line on the model; `task docs-check` fails when a run prints anything else.

## The model

[`crates/modelspec-docs/models/two_layer_relu.mspec`](https://github.com/beyond10x/modelspec/blob/main/crates/modelspec-docs/models/two_layer_relu.mspec):

```modelspec title="crates/modelspec-docs/models/two_layer_relu.mspec"
model TwoLayer {
    param w1: Tensor<f32, [4, 8]> = xavier_uniform();
    param w2: Tensor<f32, [8, 1]> = xavier_uniform();

    fn forward(x: Tensor<f32, [16, 4]>)
        -> Tensor<f32, [16, 1]> {
        let h = relu(matmul(x, w1));
        return matmul(h, w2);
    }
}

train FitTwoLayer {
    model = TwoLayer;
    input x: Tensor<f32, [16, 4]>;
    target y: Tensor<f32, [16, 1]>;
    loss = mse(model.forward(x), y);
    optimizer = sgd(lr = 0.05);
    steps = 200;
    seed = 7;
    device = cpu;
}
```
